ai.definition: Neural prosthetics are implantable medical devices designed to interface directly with the brain, aiming to restore or augment sensory and motor functions that have been lost due to injury, disease, or congenital conditions.
ai.howItWorks: These devices use microelectrodes to record neural activity and stimulate neurons in response. They can be controlled by external systems such as computers or smartphones to perform tasks like restoring vision or controlling prosthetic limbs.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for advanced treatments for conditions affecting the nervous system, including paralysis, blindness, hearing loss, and neurological disorders.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves precise microfabrication techniques to create biocompatible electrodes and encapsulation materials. These devices must be tested rigorously to ensure safety and efficacy before clinical trials.
ai.buildProcess: Components are fabricated using semiconductor processes for the electronics and biocompatible polymers or metals for the physical structure. Testing includes biological compatibility assessments, mechanical strength tests, and in vitro and in vivo performance evaluations.
ai.costDrivers: High development costs due to complex fabrication techniques, extensive clinical testing requirements, and specialized medical expertise. Long-term care and maintenance also contribute significantly to overall costs.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to grow as more successful clinical trials are conducted, leading to broader adoption and further advancements in functionality and integration with other technologies like AI.
ai.regulation: Regulated by medical device standards such as ISO 13485 for quality management systems. Clinical trials must comply with FDA (or equivalent) guidelines before market approval.
ai.risks: Includes risks associated with long-term implantation, potential infection, and the complexity of integrating these devices into existing neural networks without causing damage.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain due to high initial costs and limited market penetration. However, successful commercialization could lead to substantial revenue streams from sales and ongoing service fees.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more advanced materials for better integration, wireless power and data transmission capabilities, and improved algorithms for neural decoding and stimulation.

glossary.def: Tiny electrodes used to record or stimulate individual neurons.
Materials that are safe and compatible with biological systems, minimizing adverse reactions in the body.
A device that can communicate directly with neural tissue, either recording or stimulating activity.

subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: the actual contact with nervous tissue — recording spikes or delivering charge.
parts: cochlear electrode array inserted into the inner ear

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplify tiny neural voltages and generate stimulation pulses.

subsystems.name: Hermetic package and body
subsystems.role: seals electronics against salt water and the immune system for years.

subsystems.name: Power and data link
subsystems.role: gets energy and signals in and out through intact skin.

subsystems.name: Decoder and control software
subsystems.role: turns a pattern of neural activity into a command, or a command into a stimulation pattern.

subsystems.name: External wearable
subsystems.role: the part the user wears or carries.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target and electrode geometry
buildSteps.detail: Engineers map the tissue to be interfaced — cochlea, motor cortex, retina — and size contacts accordingly. A cortical Utah array, for example, is a 10×10 grid of 1.5 mm silicon shanks on a 400 µm pitch.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate in a cleanroom
buildSteps.detail: Thin metal films are patterned photolithographically on silicon, polyimide or parylene, then insulated everywhere except the contact sites.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and seal the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Chips are mounted in a titanium or ceramic case, feedthroughs are welded in, and the whole package is tested in warm saline to prove it is watertight.

buildSteps.title: Test for biocompatibility and lifetime
buildSteps.detail: Accelerated soak tests, cell-culture assays and animal implants establish that the device neither poisons tissue nor corrodes.

buildSteps.title: Validate in animals, then clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Efficacy and safety are demonstrated in animals and then in staged human trials under medical-device regulators.

buildSteps.title: Implant surgically
buildSteps.detail: A stereotactic frame or surgical robot places the array to sub-millimetre accuracy; the lead is tunnelled under the skin to a connector or coil on the skull.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate with the user
buildSteps.detail: Over weeks, the decoder is trained on the individual's neural signals, and the user learns to modulate them reliably.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and revise
buildSteps.detail: Electrode performance is tracked; scar tissue can raise impedance and reduce signal over years.

prerequisites.why: without contacts that survive in tissue, no interface lasts long enough to be useful.
sealing electronics for a decade inside a warm, salty, moving body is still the main engineering limit.
hundreds of channels of raw data cannot cross the skin through wires without infection risk.
movement intent can be decoded well; memory and mood are far less understood.

prerequisites.tech: A scientific account of memory and conscious states
prerequisites.why: there is no validated method to read, let alone copy or 'upload', a conscious state — the digital-afterlife part of this idea has no experimental basis.

pathway.milestone: cochlear implants and deep brain stimulation are routine clinical devices; motor brain-computer interfaces let a small number of paralysed people type and control robotic arms in trials
pathway.unlocks: restored hearing, tremor control and basic communication for severe paralysis.

pathway.milestone: fully implanted, wireless, higher-channel interfaces with multi-year stability — several stent-like and cortical devices are in early human trials
pathway.unlocks: everyday use without cables or a technician present.

pathway.milestone: sensory and memory prosthetics — cortical visual implants, and research programmes stimulating the hippocampus to aid memory encoding
pathway.unlocks: partial restoration of sight and of the ability to form new memories.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop implants that both read and stimulate, used for epilepsy, depression and spinal-cord injury
pathway.unlocks: treatments tuned to the individual's own neural state.
unknown — this requires discoveries in neuroscience that have not been made, and is not simply a matter of better electrodes.
